name: How do installers handle uneven walls and ceilings when installing crown molding?

mainEntity.name: How do installers handle uneven walls and ceilings when installing crown molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Carpenters handle crooked walls by scribing the molding directly to the wall contour. A compass or scribe tool traces the drywall's uneven profile onto the back edge of the trim board, which is then cut with a jigsaw, plane, or belt sander. For crown molding meeting an uneven ceiling, an extra backer board or flat fascia board is often installed first. This allows the crown to remain level along its top edge while the backer absorbs the ceiling height variations, preventing distorted, twisting corner joints.
acceptedAnswer.description: Installers use scribing tools to cut trim to wall contours and install flat backer boards behind crown molding to absorb ceiling height variances.
